request.spec:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be shared, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What was added**
- **Storage:** a new migration `V122__claim_share.sql` adds a `claim_share` table, mapped as `ClaimShare` and attached to `Claim` the same way claim lines are.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{id}/claims/{claimId}/shares`, backed by `ClaimService.share`. It refuses a share of 0.00 or less, a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim, the claim's own person, a person who already holds a share, and shares totalling more than 100.00. A refusal writes nothing. When a share goes through it writes `CLAIM_SHARED … with=<name> share=<share>` (plus `for=` when acting by delegation), followed by the usual ROLLUP and TOTALS lines.
- **Due-totals:** each holder's part is the claim's due × share / 100, rounded half to even. Holders get their part and the claim's own person keeps the rest. The server does this in `Dues`/`Rollup` (which write the audit lines); the screen does the same in `people-list.ts` for due-total, settled-total and open-total. The due shown on the claim itself and the "claimed" amount don't change.
- **Screen:** each claim row has a person select, a share percent field and a Share button. It shows the holders as `Ben 33.33, Cam 33.33` in the order the shares were given. Errors appear in the claim's existing error message.

**Choices the request didn't settle**
- Overdue-totals and the age buckets still go wholly to the claim's own person, since the request only named due, settled and open totals. The sheet-wide age totals come out the same either way.
- A share held by someone later merged or transferred off the sheet is ignored. The holder column has no foreign key, so those moves still work.
- Shares aren't copied when a claim is transferred or cloned to another sheet. They also aren't kept in the sheet's history, so the as-of view doesn't apply them to totals.

**One fix outside the share feature:** scenario 1 failed on something unrelated. With the sheet shown as of 2026-03-05, vic appeared as a steward through wes's delegation, but wes was only made a steward on 2026-03-10. I changed `RoleService.roleOn`, which only feeds the as-of "my role" lookup, so a delegation only makes someone a steward on days when the person delegating was already one. Revert it if you'd rather keep this change to shares only.
